messages:
support-ana: FYI customer reported an invoice where token usage is ~3x less than our dashboard for a streaming endpoint. Customer says they aborted the stream midway.
ryan-cust: @support-ana we saw the UI show ~18k tokens for the session but the invoice line item is 6k. sent logs + request id.
support-ana: k, attaching request id 0x9f3a and the customer's minimal repro. They aborted after receiving 3 partial chunks.
devon: can you paste the raw SSE chunks? curious if we didn't emit finalization metadata so metering skipped remainder.
support-ana: here are the relevant server logs (trimmed):
```
[2025-11-02T14:12:02Z] req=0x9f3a start stream model=gpt-redwood-small
[2025-11-02T14:12:05Z] req=0x9f3a chunk=1 tokens_out=120
[2025-11-02T14:12:06Z] req=0x9f3a chunk=2 tokens_out=240
[2025-11-02T14:12:07Z] req=0x9f3a chunk=3 tokens_out=180
[2025-11-02T14:12:07Z] client aborted, code=ECONNRESET
[2025-11-02T14:12:07Z] meter: session 0x9f3a recorded_total=540
[2025-11-02T14:12:07Z] billing-queue enqueue invoice-event partial=false
```
ryan-cust: I have the client trace. we cancel the fetch after we got the 3rd event.
```
const controller = new AbortController();
fetch('/v1/streams', { signal: controller.signal });
// ... on some chunk
controller.abort();
```
support-ana: customer says dashboard (live usage) shows 18k because they had a previous identical call that finished normally earlier in the session; invoices show lower because billing pipeline grouped by finalization events.
maya: interesting — billing pipeline expects an end-of-stream event to finalize per-request token aggregates. if client cancels mid-flight we fall back to meter totals we saw in the storage layer. that should still match the dashboard, though.
devon: two possible causes: 1) the ingest layer emits incremental token deltas but the downstream billing consumer ignores increments for streaming endpoints unless it sees final=true, or 2) some chunks are buffered and not crystalized into meter records before the abort and are lost.
-ingest-pkg: tagging in: our SSE adapter flushes buffer every 250ms or on end. if the client abort happens between flushes those buffered tokens are lost unless the runtime forces a flush on connection error.
ryan-cust: is there any idempotency or metadata we can attach to avoid losses? we need accurate invoicing.
maya: short-term we can credit the delta while we root cause. long-term fix required in ingest or meter consumer.
devon: quick repro I used to simulate: curl to SSE, then kill connection after N events
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-redwood-small
# wait ~2s then ctrl-c
```
```
# server saw 5 chunks, meter recorded 520 tokens, dashboard shows 520, invoice shows 120 (buggy consumer)
```
maya: ok that's a smoking gun. billing consumer sometimes replays an earlier checkpoint if it races with a partial commit. i'll open a billing-consumer ticket.
devon: possible quick patch: make ingest emit a final flush on connection error and include an explicit event: `{ "type": "stream_end", "final_token_count": 520 }`. that lets downstream consumers reconcile even if they missed deltas.
-ingest-pkg: we can add that in the adapter; low-risk change. will take ~1 day + QA.
maya: request we also add a consumer-side guard: if an invoice event's token total is dramatically lower than recent dashboard values for the same session/customer, hold and flag for manual review before billing. threshold e.g., >2x diff.
support-ana: customer asked for timeline and temporary mitigation.
maya: propose: 1) immediate credit for the delta (we'll issue a $XX credit) 2) hotfix to ingest to flush on abort (deploy in 24-48h) 3) consumer guard + longer term robust reconciliation (2 weeks).
ryan-cust: credit appreciated. timeline ok. please keep me updated.
devon: I'll prototype the flush-and-end-event patch and post a PR by EOD. will include unit test that simulates abort during buffered window.
-ingest-pkg: noted. I'll coordinate rollout and smoke tests. can we add a small integration test that uses the curl abort flow?
devon: yes. also logging hooks so meter emits `final_token_count` for every stream.
maya: billing will also run a one-off script to reconcile invoices for past 7 days where invoices < dashboard * 0.6 for streaming endpoints. we'll flag affected customers for credits.
support-ana: great. I've informed the customer and filed SR-4531 for the credit. adding owners: @devon (ingest patch), @ingest-pkg (adapter rollout), @maya (billing reconciliation).
billing-bot: Invoice SR-4531 created. ETA for credit: 2 business days.
support-ana: thanks all. will update thread when PR merges or credit issued. :thumbsup:
